text:
Alex Kim: Quick sync — I sketched failure-mode scenarios we should validate before committing the multi-region rollout window. want to align on launch gates.
Maya Patel: +1. Can you call out which scenarios you mean?
Alex Kim: Short list: 1) full-region outage, 2) degraded cross-region bandwidth (packet loss), 3) partial control-plane isolation (API sync lag), 4) tenant migration during failover, 5) KV cache corruption edge.
Jon Reed: Also add: model-variant mismatch during fallback (fp16 vs int8) causing quality regressions. customer reported this in staging last week.
Maya Patel: Good call. For each scenario we should have an SLO failure budget impact estimate and an automated playbook.
Priya Sinha: For launch gating I propose: p95 gen latency <200ms inside-region, failover completion <60s, model-output regression <2% on critical prompts, and telemetry coverage (trace + token-level cost) enabled. thoughts?
Leah Gomez: 60s seems long for some customers. Can we make it 45s for platinum tiers and 90s for self-serve?
Alex Kim: Agree on tiers. We'll codify routing policy precedence: 1) local region, 2) dedicated pool fallback, 3) cross-region fallback (with canary), 4) degraded-mode (lower-cost quantized variant).
ops-bot: deploy-candidate:policy/geo-fallbacks v0.3 deployed to sandbox at 2024-10-11T15:22:04Z :information_source:
Jon Reed: Shared a small policy snippet to illustrate the canary flow:```yaml
routing_policy:
  precedence:
    - region: primary
    - pool: dedicated
    - region: canary
  canary:
    sample_rate: 0.01
    metrics: [latency_p95, quality_regressions]
  degraded_mode:
    allowed_variants: [quantized-8bit, distill-small]
    qos_budget: 0.15
```
Maya Patel: For canary metrics: we need automated rollback thresholds. e.g. latency_p95 +10% OR quality_regressions > 1% for 5m -> rollback.
Priya Sinha: Also add cost-signal: if per-token cost increases >25% during canary for >10m -> pause canary.
Leah Gomez: Ops runbook needs these steps: 1) detect, 2) switch routing precedence to dedicated, 3) pin affected tenants to previous model, 4) run remediation script, 5) notify CS and sales. Keep it short.
Alex Kim: Agreed. Who owns the runbook and the remediation scripts?
Jon Reed: I'll own remediation scripts for model-variant issues. Priya can own automation for cost- and latency-based canary gating.
Priya Sinha: Yup I can take canary gating automation. I need a telemetry contract from platform: events, token-level cost, and per-tenant quality signals.
Maya Patel: Product asks: include a launch criterion for customer migration window communication (at least 72h notice for planned cutovers affecting dedicated pools).
Alex Kim: Action items: 1) Jon -> remediation scripts by next Wed (1777800000). 2) Priya -> canary gating automation prototype in 2 sprints. 3) Leah -> Ops runbook draft and escalation matrix. 4) Maya -> update customer-facing migration policy.
Leah Gomez: I'll also add a small playbook snippet for emergency tenant quarantine commands (one-liners we can run from console).
Jon Reed: Example quarantine command (for console run):```bash
redwoodctl tenant quarantine --tenant-id T-1234 --region us-west-2 --reason "failover-induced quality regression"
```
Alex Kim: Nice. One more cross-cut: telemetry thresholds and the list of critical prompts used for quality checks. Research/ML needs to publish a canonical prompt set for each tier. Priya, can you coordinate?
Priya Sinha: Yes, I'll sync with ML and publish the prompt sets.
Maya Patel: Timeline check — can we aim for a limited pilot (10 customers, mixed tiers) in 6 weeks from now?
Alex Kim: That seems reasonable if remediation scripts + canary automation land on time. We’ll treat pilot as an experiment with rollback by default.
ops-bot: reminder: weekly-ops-sync in #eng-oncall tomorrow 09:00 PST :calendar:
Leah Gomez: I'll post a short pre-read with the runbook and policy snippet by EOD Friday.
Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — I'll capture this in the roadmap doc and ping sales for candidate pilot customers.
Alex Kim: Closing: main gating checklist -> telemetry yes, canary automation yes, remediation scripts yes, customer notice policy in place. If any objections, respond in thread. :thumbsup:
